name: Miami-Dade County Commission

meetings.pattern: Regular meetings on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 9:30 a.m. (the rules say first and third Tuesday and Thursday, but the posted calendar uses Tuesdays, with a carry-over day the next morning if needed). Zoning and master-plan (CDMP) meetings about once a month on a Thursday at 9:30 a.m. Committees meet the second week of the month. All in the Commission Chambers, 2nd floor, Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st Street, Miami 33128. Meetings end no later than 6:30 p.m.

Committees: Appropriations 9:00, Intergovernmental and Economic Impact 10:30, Infrastructure Innovation and Technology 12:30

phases.name: Departments submit budget requests
phases.decides: County departments send business plans and budget requests to the Office of Management and Budget; the Mayor gives a budget address in March setting priorities.

phases.name: Mayor's proposed budget and tentative tax rates
phases.decides: Property Appraiser certifies taxable values by July 1; the Mayor must deliver the proposed budget to the Commission by July 15 (County Code); the Commission sets the tentative millage rates that go on the August TRIM notices.

phases.name: TRIM notices and fee meetings
phases.decides: Notices of proposed property taxes are mailed to every owner; public meetings are held around the county on proposed new or increased fees and taxes.

phases.name: Two public budget hearings
phases.decides: Two evening hearings at 5:01 p.m. The second hearing sets final tax rates, adopts the budget ordinances, the fee schedules and the pay plan. 2026 hearings were Sept 3 and Sept 17; 2027 proposed dates are Sept 9 and Sept 23.

phases.name: Fiscal year begins
phases.decides: The adopted budget takes effect; the fiscal year runs Oct 1 to Sept 30. Supplemental appropriations usually come at mid-year and year-end.

phases.name: General election (runoffs for county races)
phases.decides: Runoffs for Commission Districts 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 where no candidate won a majority in the Aug 18 primary; also county charter questions.

phases.name: New terms begin
phases.decides: Commissioners elected in 2026 take office the second Tuesday after the general election (Charter Sec. 3.01(C)).

phases.name: Winter recess
phases.decides: No full-board or zoning meetings are posted after Nov 19, 2026; only Dec 3 committee meetings. The calendar legend lists spring, summer and winter recess without exact dates.

phases.name: Spring break
phases.decides: No meetings (proposed 2027 calendar; 2026 spring break was Mar 23-27).

levers.how: Speak on any public hearing item: register at the Agenda Coordination table in the chamber lobby (first floor) at least 15 minutes before the item is called; you are escorted to the chambers. State your name, address and whom you represent.
levers.rules: Up to 5 minutes per speaker on a public hearing item (Rule 6.04). Public hearings are scheduled for 9:30 a.m. You may also waive your time 'in support' or 'in opposition'.
levers.deadline: Register at the meeting, at least 15 minutes before the item is discussed

levers.how: Speak on any other agenda item (not a public hearing) during the 'reasonable opportunity to be heard' period under Rule 6.06, which comes near the start of the meeting before the agenda is set. Register with a speaker card the morning of the meeting.
levers.rules: 2 minutes per speaker, 10 minutes total per side; if more than five people sign up on one side they pick a representative who gets 4 minutes. No one may speak more than 5 minutes total on one agenda. Registration closes 30 minutes after the noticed start time.
levers.deadline: Register by 10:00 a.m. for a 9:30 a.m. meeting

levers.how: Citizens' presentation: ask your commissioner or the Mayor to place you on the regular meeting agenda to speak on any matter in the Commission's power. Only a commissioner or the Mayor can place you.
levers.rules: 5 minutes maximum (agenda item 1E). The Commission cannot act on it unless two thirds of members present agree it needs immediate action.
levers.deadline: Request to a commissioner by noon on the Monday of the week before the meeting week

levers.how: Budget hearings: come to the Commission Chambers at 5:01 p.m. on the two September hearing dates and register to speak on the first floor.
levers.rules: Register on the first floor; speakers are escorted to the chambers. Accommodation requests to agendco@miamidade.gov or 305-375-2035 in advance.

levers.how: No formal written-comment channel is posted in the rules. Write to your district commissioner (DistrictN@miamidade.gov) and the Chair; for zoning items, email presentation materials to the Development Services Division before the hearing with the Z-number.
levers.rules: Zoning materials: PowerPoint, 100 MB max, become public record and are shown only while you speak. Emails to commissioners are public records.

levers.how: Find your district on the Commission home page (13 district pages) or the Services Near You map, then email the district office. Each office also has a Stephen P. Clark Center suite and phone.
levers.rules: Email pattern DistrictN@miamidade.gov (no leading zero), for example District1@miamidade.gov, 305-375-5694.

levers.how: Request Commission records (minutes, resolutions, ordinances, backup) through the county public records portal, choosing 'Board of County Commission', or email the Clerk of the Board.
levers.rules: Requests get a control number and acknowledgment; processed in order received; a cost estimate is given if applicable. Questions: 305-593-1352.

levers.how: Initiative or referendum (Charter Sec. 8.01): electors may propose passing or repealing a county ordinance. Get the petition form approved by the Clerk of the Circuit Court, then collect signatures.
levers.rules: Signatures equal to at least 4 percent of registered county voters, with no more than 25 percent from any one commission district, collected within 120 days of the form's approval. The Board orders a canvass within 30 days of filing and may adopt the ordinance within 30 days of a sufficient petition; otherwise it goes to the ballot. With 8 percent of voters the election is held the first Tuesday after 120 days from certification; otherwise at the next countywide election. Majority vote; effective the day after the election. Signature checks follow Code Sec. 12-23.
levers.deadline: 120 days from approval of the petition form

levers.how: Charter amendment by petition (Charter Sec. 9.07): electors may put a charter amendment on the ballot.
levers.rules: Signatures of at least 10 percent of registered electors in the county. The Board must call an election 60 to 120 days after a certified petition is presented. The Board may also propose amendments itself at any time.

levers.how: Recall of the Mayor or a commissioner (Charter Sec. 8.02): get the petition form approved by the Clerk of the Circuit Court, collect signatures, and file for canvass and certification.
levers.rules: Signatures of at least 4 percent of registered voters in the county (for the Mayor) or the district (for a commissioner), collected within 120 days of form approval. No recall petition may be certified within one year after the officer takes office or within one year after a prior recall against them failed. The Board must set the recall election 45 to 90 days after certification.
levers.deadline: 120 days from approval of the petition form

levers.how: Run for Commission: file qualifying papers with the Supervisor of Elections during the qualifying window in the election year, paying the fee or filing petition signatures.
levers.rules: 2026: qualifying 8:00 a.m. May 26 to noon June 9; fee $360 (write-in $300); or petition signatures equal to 1 percent of district voters due noon April 28. Must be a county resident 3 years and district resident 6 months before qualifying (Charter Sec. 1.04). Two consecutive four-year term limit (Sec. 3.01(E)).
levers.deadline: Noon on the last day of qualifying (June 9 in 2026; 2028 dates not yet posted)

levers.how: County commissioners are elected by district in the August primary of even years; if no one wins a majority, the top two go to a runoff on the November general election ballot.
levers.rules: Even-numbered districts (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) in 2026; odd districts and the Mayor on the 2028 cycle. Nonpartisan.
levers.deadline: Nov 3, 2026 runoffs; register 29 days before an election

levers.how: Apply for a seat on a county advisory board through the County Boards and Appointment System (CBAS), which lists active boards, vacancies and liaison contacts. Appointments are made by commissioners or the Mayor.
levers.rules: Service is voluntary and unpaid; eligibility rules are in County Code Secs. 2-11.36.1 through 2-11.38.2. Clerk of the Board 305-275-1155.

levers.how: Zoning: Community Zoning Appeals Boards (CZABs) hold evening hearings by area (for example CZAB 2 met Sept 22, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. at Highland Oaks Park). Anyone may speak. Zone changes, certain use variances and administrative-decision appeals decided by a CZAB can be appealed to the County Commission.
levers.rules: Appeal to the Commission within 14 days after the CZAB result is posted on the appeals log; fee $855 ($923.40 with surcharge); file in person at the Public Hearing Section, Stephen P. Clark Center 11th floor, by 4:30 p.m.; applicant, aggrieved party of record, affected city, or neighborhood association may appeal. Questions 305-375-2640.
levers.deadline: 14 days after the CZAB decision is posted

elections.terms: Four years, staggered: even districts (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) elected in 2026, odd districts (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13) and the Mayor in 2028. Primary in August, runoff in November, term starts the second Tuesday after the November election. Limit of two consecutive four-year terms (terms begun before 2012 do not count).
